cases.title: Thread Message Context Menu / Default Message

summary: Context menu is rendered as a portal/popover anchored to the message on React but appears as an inline stacked block below the message on Android, causing large layout drift.
Android menu has 7 items including a 'Select Text' entry plus an extra 'Follow Thread' on React that becomes its own grouped section; React shows 7 items with 'Select Message' and no 'Select Text'.

React groups emoji reactions inside the popover and places Copy Link/Copy Markdown/Select Message in one block, then Open Thread/Save Message/Follow Thread in another; Android splits Copy Link/Copy Markdown/Select Text/Select Message into a single block and Open Thread/Save Message into another, with Convert to Task isolated.
React's menu is narrower (icon rail ~32px, total width ~280px) while Android's menu is wider (~360px) and uses larger row heights and padding.

Section dividers are thick black bars on React but appear as hairline 1px rules on Android, and React uses bolder/larger label typography (≈16px/600) versus Android's lighter/smaller labels (≈14px/regular).
likelyCauses: Android Compose implementation re-implemented the menu as a stacked column of cards rather than as a single floating popover anchored to the message bubble.

Different component primitive used on Android (Card/OutlinedButton rows vs. React's Menu/Popover), producing mismatched paddings, dividers, and font metrics.
Token mismatch for spacing/radius/elevation between design system web and Compose themes.

Description field on Android renders as a single-line input instead of a multi-line textarea; placeholder text "Build reports, screenshots, release" is clipped/truncated with no wrap (React wraps to two lines and shows a resize handle).
Agent and human list rows on Android include a secondary meta line (e.g. "agent · @Cindy", "human · @designer") that is absent in React rows, increasing row height and adding avatars+text per item.
Spacing between form sections (label-to-input, input-to-label) is larger on Android, especially around VISIBILITY and MEMBERS.
The pink checkmark indicators for selected members are present on both but are positioned differently due to row-height change; Android checks sit further right within taller rows.
likelyCauses: Android implementation maps the Description field to a single-line TextInput instead of a multi-line TextArea.
Android Member/Agent list item template renders two lines (primary name + secondary handle/role) vs React's single-line template.
Android applies larger vertical padding/margin on form labels, inputs, and list rows than the React design tokens specify.
Dialog body on Android uses fillViewportHeight or wrapContent with extra padding, while React constrains dialog height to content.
suggestedFixes: Replace the single-line EditText for Description with a multi-line input (inputType="textMultiLine") and minLines/tall enough to show wrapped placeholder text.
Reduce member list row template on Android to a single primary line (or make the secondary meta line optional/hidden by default) to match React row height.
Normalize vertical spacing tokens (label margin, input height, section gap) to match React values; audit dimens.xml for form spacing.
Constrain the Android dialog max height so it doesn't fill the viewport when content is short, or apply scrolling inside the dialog body.
Verify the pink selection checkmark alignment still reads correctly after row-height normalization.
intentional: Pink "Create Channel" primary button color and selected-member row tint appear consistent across both platforms.

summary: The Android version shows a different error banner text ('Failed to create agent') vs React's 'Agent limit reached (2/2 on Free plan). Upgrade for more', indicating a wrong/different error state is being rendered.
Android renders an extra 'Suggested computer: computer-mbp' helper line under the COMPUTER select that is absent in React.

The MODE section differs: React shows 'Fast mode' inside a bordered card with helper text 'Launch this runtime with its faster service/minimal mode.', while Android shows a plain checkbox with no helper text and no card, plus an 'Advanced' disclosure row that React does not display.

Android displays a footer action bar with 'Cancel' and 'Create Agent' (primary, pink) buttons at the bottom of the viewport; React's version cuts off after MODE with no visible footer buttons, suggesting the dialog is taller/longer than the viewport on React or the footer is missing on the React baseline.

Form field vertical density/spacing differs: React fields (NAME, DESCRIPTION, RUNTIME, MODEL, REASONING) are spaced further apart and the DESCRIPTION textarea is taller; Android compresses spacing and uses a shorter DESCRIPTION box.
likelyCauses: Android implementation is rendering a different error state than the React baseline (failure message vs limit-reached upsell).
Android added/changed helper text ('Suggested computer', 'Advanced') that the React component does not emit.
React dialog may be missing the action footer (Cancel/Create Agent) or the baseline capture is clipped before the footer, while Android correctly renders it within the viewport.
Inconsistent design-token mapping on Android: spacing scale, label typography weight, and card vs flat surface treatments were not ported from the React spec.
Optional helper/description copy under the Fast mode checkbox was dropped or not implemented in the Android Compose component.
suggestedFixes: Align the Android error banner copy/state with React: render the 'Agent limit reached (2/2 on Free plan). Upgrade for more' message and remove the 'Failed to create agent' placeholder when the limit-exceeded condition holds.
Remove or gate the 'Suggested computer' line so it only appears when the React spec shows it; verify the same data hook drives both clients.
Reconcile MODE section: either remove the 'Advanced' row on Android or add it (with matching label) to React; keep 'Fast mode' helper text and card surface consistent across platforms.
Verify the action footer (Cancel / Create Agent) is rendered on React and that the baseline capture region includes the full modal height so the buttons are not clipped.
Normalize typography and spacing tokens between platforms: label uppercase weight, '(optional)' sizing, field vertical gap, and DESCRIPTION textarea min-height should match the React spec.

summary: React baseline shows a pink/cream 'Agent limit reached (2/2 on Free plan). Upgrade for more' banner directly below the 'CREATE AGENT' header; Android current does not show this limit-reached banner at all.
Android current shows a 'Suggested computer: computer-mbp' hint directly beneath the COMPUTER select; this helper text is absent on the React baseline.

Android current shows Cancel and Create Agent action buttons anchored bottom-right inside the dialog; React baseline's buttons are not visible in the cropped viewport (the form scrolls past them on the baseline while Android renders them inline).

Android current is vertically compressed/zoomed vs the React baseline: form labels and inputs are rendered at a smaller scale, causing the whole content to fit above the action buttons, whereas the React layout lets the form flow off-screen and Reason field is clipped at the bottom.
Form field vertical spacing on Android is noticeably tighter than on React; gaps between COMPUTER, NAME, DESCRIPTION, RUNTIME, PROVIDER, MODEL and REASONING are reduced on the Android side.
likelyCauses: Android Compose implementation skipped the limit-reached warning banner state/conditional render that the React version shows.
Android implementation adds an extra suggested-computer hint element not present in the React spec.
Action button row (Cancel/Create Agent) was added/promoted into the visible dialog area on Android instead of being in a sticky footer or below the scrollable form as on React.

Missing or different scroll container/scale settings on Android: scale-to-fit or different padding/scale causes fields to render smaller and the Cancel/Create Agent buttons to become visible rather than scrolled-off.
Unit/density differences (dp vs px) and layout compression make Android content fit where React content overflows.
suggestedFixes: Add the same 'Agent limit reached (2/2 on Free plan). Upgrade for more' warning banner component in Android, conditionally rendered when the user is on the Free plan with 2/2 agents, matching color, weight and copy of the React version.
Remove the 'Suggested computer: computer-mbp' helper text from the Android COMPUTER field if it is not part of the design, or add it to the React baseline if it is intended.

Match React layout/scroll behavior: keep Cancel and Create Agent either pinned in a sticky footer or outside the scrollable form so the Reason field isn't pushed off-screen; do not auto-scale the form down to force buttons into view.

Align vertical spacing between form fields and labels with the React baseline (increase dp padding between sections) so COMPUTER→NAME→DESCRIPTION→RUNTIME→PROVIDER→MODEL→REASONING gaps are visually consistent.
Verify typography scale and density: use the same font size/sp/dp scale as React so inputs, labels, and helper text match the React renders rather than appearing shrunken.
intentional: Android dialog composites the form and action buttons within a single viewport rather than letting the form overflow, which may be an intentional responsive choice but conflicts with React's behavior.

summary: Different layout density: Android uses a more compact, stacked layout with merged/shorter section headers, while React uses larger, separated cards with more whitespace.

Section header style differs: React shows 'CONNECTED APPS' and 'BUILT-IN' as small uppercase labels in muted color above cards; Android replaces these with inline section icons and titles ('Connected Apps', 'Built-in') plus subtitle text under the page title.

Counter/pill representation differs: React renders 'Marketplace 3 / Installed 2 / My apps 1' as combined labeled pills; Android splits these into separate numeric tiles ('3', '2', '1') with labels beneath, then a secondary row of icon-prefixed tabs.

App card action button variant differs: React 'Open' button is solid pink with no icon; Android 'Open' button adds an external-link icon next to the label. 'Install' (React) vs 'Details' (Android) labels differ for the same card slot.

Iconography and typography weight: Android uses outlined leading icons (link, store, check, key) and lighter body type for descriptions; React uses plain bordered tiles with bold titles and no leading icons.
likelyCauses: Different component libraries / design-system implementations between web (React) and native (Android) targets producing divergent visual defaults.
Independent re-implementation of the Connected Apps page in Android rather than shared design tokens, leading to restructured information hierarchy.
Varied interpretation of spec for counter/pill groupings and section labeling.
suggestedFixes: Define and share a single visual contract (tokens) for section labels, counter pills, and card actions across React and Android implementations.
Unify header treatment: decide whether a subtitle under 'Connected Apps' belongs in both platforms and render consistently.
Standardize the numeric counters (Marketplace/Installed/My apps) — either as combined pills (React) or as numeric tiles (Android) — and apply the chosen pattern everywhere.

cases.title: Thread Message Row Long Inline Code

summary: Avatar and timestamp row layout differs: React shows avatar at far left with a clear gap before 'Cindy' name and a truncated 'Keeps vis… 06/25 05:55 AM' subtitle; Android shows the avatar inline at left with a single-line subtitle 'Keeps visual testing … 06/25 05:55' that extends further right.

Body text wraps to different column widths: React renders at a wider body width so long inline-code paths wrap on fewer, longer lines; Android renders at a noticeably narrower effective text width, causing more frequent line breaks in the long path and the gradlew command blocks.

Long inline-code spans break at different points: React keeps the path and command as a single continuous yellow box wrapping at the container edge; Android splits the yellow fill into separate adjacent boxes (visible gap/border between segments such as 'raft.build.markdown' and '.inlineCode', and between 'owner-key' and '-consumes-thread-route'), producing a visually segmented wrap.

The bottom gradlew command block is clipped/cropped on Android — the final line 'visual.KmpVisualScreenshotCapture' is cut off at the canvas bottom (390×844), whereas on React the same content fits within bounds (final visible line is '.captureThreadMessageRowLongInlineCode.').
Right-side metadata badge uses different casing/label: 'REACT' (green) on the left vs 'ANDROID' (yellow) on the right — expected but worth noting for test screenshot consistency.
likelyCauses: Android markdown/inline-code renderer treats each visual line of a wrapped code span as a separate background-painted box rather than a single rounded background that flows across line breaks.
Android text container width is smaller (different horizontal padding or avatar/text-column geometry) causing the long code blocks to wrap at shorter line lengths.
Canvas height (844pt) is insufficient for the Android layout's taller line count, resulting in bottom-edge clipping of the last gradlew command line.
suggestedFixes: Make Android paint a single continuous yellow code-span background across wrapped lines (or merge adjacent code-span backgrounds) so wrapped paths look like one chip like React.
Reconcile avatar/text-column padding on Android to match React's body width, or reduce body horizontal insets so long inline code has more room before wrapping.
Extend test canvas height or shorten fixture content so the final gradlew command line is not clipped on Android; alternatively cap content to fit 844pt on both platforms.
Verify the metadata badge color/label scheme (REACT green / ANDROID yellow) is intentional and consistent across visual-test baselines.
intentional: @KMP-专家 is rendered as an underlined @mention chip on Android but as plain text on React — intentional platform difference (Android tags all @mentions regardless of resolution).
Bare #520 is rendered as a yellow task chip on Android and as plain text on React — intentional platform difference (Android tags all bare #number task refs).
Mention @artin and the #markdown专修 channel chip are tagged on both sides since they resolve to known entities — this is the intended shared behavior.

cases.title: Settings Administration Full Height Screen

summary: Android renders the Administration settings screen in a single scrollable form whereas React presents settings as discrete card-based sections, causing large vertical/structural differences (~31px taller on Android).

Header pattern differs: Android shows a back arrow + 'Administration' page title; React uses a small caption 'Settings: Administration Full-Height Screen' at the top of each card with no global title.

Owners & Admins control differs: React uses an 'Add owner/admin' select + 'Admin' select + 'Update Role' button + member list card; Android uses a single 'Control who can manage this workspace' card listing one owner with a 'Last owner' pill and no role-update UI.

System Channels differs: React has an interactive 'Hide #all channel' toggle with Save button and descriptive copy; Android shows a read-only 'System Channels' card with an 'Unavailable' status and eye icon.
Pending Invites differs: React displays invites as compact rows with a date and small X icon; Android expands each invite into a full card showing inviter email and a large 'Revoke' button.
likelyCauses: Android implementation reimplemented the Administration form as a new card-based layout instead of reusing the React component contract (different component library / native form widgets).
Different form patterns: Android uses radio groups, segmented controls, and inline cards; React uses selects, checkboxes, and inline label/input rows.
Save-button semantics differ: React uses per-section Save buttons with default disabled state; Android uses always-enabled filled buttons with leading icons.
Additional sections (Sidebar Order, Danger Zone) were added on Android but not part of the React baseline contract used for this snapshot.
Toggle/pill style: Android uses yellow-filled 'Required' pill and radio highlight; React uses simple checkbox toggles.
suggestedFixes: Reuse the React baseline contract for section structure and labels (e.g., 'Hide #all channel' toggle, 'Enable message translation', 'Hide human directory'), or update the baseline to match the new Android design and re-baseline.
Normalize Save/Update buttons: same color, same enabled-by-default behavior, same iconography, and same placement across both platforms.
Unify Onboarding control: pick either a select (React) or a radio list (Android) and apply consistently; align New Agent Greeting control (select vs segmented Yes/No).
Unify Pre-Join Agreement: choose inline title/body/preview (React) or stacked cards with character counter (Android) and apply on both.
Remove or include 'Sidebar Order' and 'Danger Zone' consistently across platforms; if platform-specific, exclude from full-height visual contract.
intentional: Sidebar Order card showing 'Unavailable' status on Android.
Danger Zone with 'Delete Server' being Android-only.
